html:
Gennady Golovkin (born 1982), known as GGG, is a boxer from Karaganda in Kazakhstan, one of the dominant middleweight champions of his era. His father was Russian and his mother a Korean, from the community descended from the Koreans deported to Central Asia in 1937. He won a silver medal at the 2004 Olympics in Athens.

He turned professional in Germany in 2006 and later fought mainly in the United States. Known for steady pressure and heavy punching, he held the WBA, WBC and IBF middleweight titles at various times and made a long run of title defences, most ending by knockout. His three fights with the Mexican Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, in 2017, 2018 and 2022, were among the biggest events in the sport: a disputed draw, a narrow defeat and a clear defeat.

He is a national hero in Kazakhstan, which has produced many boxing champions since independence, and in 2024 he was elected president of the country's National Olympic Committee.
